title: Jelly DJ: Soft-Body Sound Stage
description: A gelatinous CesiumMan stands on a wobbly soft-body platform, surrounded by BoomBox speakers that emit visible shockwaves. The user clicks BoomBoxes to fire bass pulses that deform the jelly man and his platform, then adjusts frequency sliders and drags speakers to sculpt the wobble patterns, aiming to match a target resonance shape displayed as a ghost outline.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a soft-body deformation scene. Load CesiumMan.glb at the center standing on a subdivided plane mesh (30x30 segments) acting as a soft-body platform. Load 4 instances of BoomBox.glb positioned in a circle around the man at radius 3, each elevated slightly and scaled to 80x original size. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,6) looking at origin. Lighting: warm amber DirectionalLight from above-right, cool blue HemisphereLight, and a pulsing PointLight on each BoomBox that glows when active. Soft-body system: store each vertex of the platform and CesiumMan's skinned mesh as spring-mass particles. Each vertex has velocity and a rest position. On each frame, apply spring forces pulling vertices toward rest positions (stiffness 0.03, damping 0.92). Interactions (8 steps with validation): 1) Click any BoomBox to activate it — it emits a visible expanding ring (TorusGeometry shockwave) that displaces nearby vertices outward based on inverse-square distance (validate: ring must appear and vertices must move >0.05 units). 2) Hold Shift+Click a BoomBox to set it to continuous pulse mode at 1Hz (validate: pulsing flag toggled). 3) Drag BoomBoxes around the circle with raycaster-based drag constrained to the XZ plane (validate: position actually changes). 4) A UI slider labeled 'Frequency' (0.5–4 Hz) controls pulse rate of all active speakers (validate: clamped range). 5) A 'Stiffness' slider (0.01–0.1) adjusts spring constant live (validate: parameter updates). 6) Press 'G' to toggle a translucent green ghost outline showing a target deformation shape on the platform (validate: ghost mesh visibility toggles). 7) Press 'R' to reset all vertices to rest positions with an animated ease-back over 1 second (validate: animation duration). 8) A score display compares current platform vertex positions to the ghost target using mean squared error, updated each frame. Use AnimationMixer to play CesiumMan's walk animation, with playback speed modulated by the average vertex displacement magnitude so he wobbles faster under heavy bass. Add OrbitControls for camera. All shockwave rings should fade and scale up over 1 second then dispose. Use requestAnimationFrame loop with a delta-time clock.
